headline: Three nested styled wrappers is where the styled fold gives up (the chain is aliased and folds at most one hop), so the css-prop fold that merges all three into one class ties `vanilla`, and the styled lane leans on its perf runtime instead.

microbench.why: The css-prop fold concatenates all three levels' classes onto the plain element, so `next-yak-css-9.7` renders one flat class and ties `vanilla` at 0.520 ms/1k. The styled lane cannot fold the `styled(styled(styled))` chain — it is aliased and the fold takes at most one hop — but its perf runtime collapses the three nested `Yak` renders into one wrapper at construction time, holding 0.662 ms/1k. The measure of that runtime: the 9.6.0 styled build, which renders each level as its own `Yak`, sits at 2.41 ms/1k here — 3.6× slower. The hash libraries trail further (`styled-components` 1.27 ms/1k, `panda` 9.69 ms/1k).

autocannon.why: Under load the single-class css-prop fold matches `vanilla`; the styled lane's perf-collapsed wrapper costs it ~20% (1282 vs 1546 req/s), and the hash libraries fall to `emotion` 412 req/s.

attribution.why: The css-prop fold's library slice is 0.083 ms — three levels merged into one class, nothing to render — tying `vanilla`. The styled lane's 0.171 ms lib is the single residual `Yak` the perf runtime leaves after collapsing the chain; the 9.6.0 build spends 1.50 ms in lib here running three `Yak` bodies per element. `panda`'s css-fn is 10.6 ms of component self-time.

hydrate.why: Extracted lanes hydrate as pure JS at ~45-47 ms. Folding matters on the client too: with it disabled the css-prop chain keeps its wrappers and hydration jumps to 87.2 ms, near the runtime libraries (`styled-components` 104 ms), showing the fold removes real client work, not just SSR cost.

inp.why: A single composed update is ~7-8 ms across the field within the interaction spread. `panda` (34.7 ms) is the outlier, walking its style path per level on the re-render.

mount.why: The css-prop fold's flat tree mounts fastest; the runtime libraries add first-inject (`styled-components` 97.7 ms, `emotion` 102 ms, `panda` 115 ms).

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every approach — parity; the styleMs spread is sub-millisecond.

payload.why: The css-prop fold merges three levels into one class and ships smallest (2.66 kB gz); the styled lane carries the wrapper chain (3.88 kB); the runtime and utility lanes are 3.6-4.2× larger (`styled-components` 16.3 kB).

nsweep.why: At 4000 three-level elements the css-prop fold and `vanilla` stay flat (~2.1 ms); the styled lane's residual wrapper adds ~0.5 ms, and the 9.6.0 build (which renders three `Yak` bodies each) compounds to 9.71 ms — the perf runtime is what keeps 9.7.0 flat.

crossCase: In the `compose-1`/`compose-3`/`compose-6` sweep, `compose-3` is the turning point: the styled fold that led `compose-1` stops resolving the chain here, so the css-prop fold (one merged class) and the perf runtime (one collapsed wrapper) carry 9.7.0. The 9.6.0 build's 2.41 ms/1k against 9.7.0's 0.662 ms/1k is the release gain the perf runtime delivers on this exact shape.
